display_title: Markets Slide as Oil and Yields Surge
display_title_he: השווקים יורדים על רקע זינוק בנפט ובתשואות האג"ח
short_summary: Global stock markets faced downward pressure as crude oil prices surged past $104 and US Treasury yields neared multi-decade highs, overshadowing major corporate developments in AI and hardware.

paragraphs: Global financial markets are experiencing a pronounced period of volatility, driven by a potent combination of surging energy prices, multi-decade highs in government bond yields, and geopolitical anxieties. On Wall Street, major stock indices have pointed downward, with futures indicating a continuation of recent losses. This negative sentiment has reverberated across European and Asian bourses, as investors grapple with a rapidly changing macroeconomic landscape.

A primary catalyst for the market's unease is the dramatic spike in crude oil prices. Brent crude has surged past the $104 per barrel threshold, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) has climbed above $91.50. This energy rally is fueled by escalating geopolitical friction in the Middle East, particularly following reports that the White House has asked the Pentagon to draft options for potential military strikes against Iran. Additionally, a tanker attack off the coast of Qatar, intensified Houthi strikes against Saudi Arabia, and production halts by Shell and Chevron in the Gulf of Mexico due to an approaching tropical storm have severely heightened supply disruption fears.

Concurrently, the bond market is exerting significant pressure on equities. The yield on the benchmark 10-year US Treasury note has crept back toward 5.33%, hovering near levels not seen since 2002. Meanwhile, the 30-year yield has crossed 5.71%. High yields offer a compelling alternative to equities, prompting Savita Subramanian of Bank of America to note that, for the first time in decades, stock markets face a genuine rival in bonds. Billionaire investor Ray Dalio, founder of Bridgewater, also issued a stark warning, advising market participants to focus on deteriorating free cash flow rather than superficial corporate earnings, declaring that the market is firmly entrenched in a bond bear market.

Despite these headwinds, the US labor market remains remarkably resilient. Weekly jobless claims fell to 197,000, underscoring a tight employment environment. This strength may embolden the Federal Reserve to maintain its hawkish stance. Fed Governor Christopher Waller signaled that further interest rate hikes remain on the table to steer inflation back to the central bank's 2% target.

In corporate news, several major technology players are navigating distinct shifts. Palantir received a substantial boost after Goldman Sachs upgraded its rating to "Buy" with a target price of $230, citing the global transition toward "Sovereign AI." Conversely, Broadcom shares dipped slightly following reports that it is coordinating over $50 billion in financing to develop custom artificial intelligence chips for OpenAI.

Meanwhile, Amazon announced a strategic pivot in its hardware division under CEO Andy Jassy. The e-commerce giant is abandoning its budget-friendly Fire tablet line in favor of a premium Alexa-branded series priced between $230 and $550. These new devices will run on Android rather than Fire OS and feature advanced "On-Screen Intelligence" tools. In the semiconductor sector, Wolfspeed shares skyrocketed over 15% after securing a $1.5 billion, 30-year loan commitment from the Pentagon to bolster domestic manufacturing. Lastly, Samsung Electronics reported a ninefold surge in quarterly operating profit to $80 billion, yet its stock slipped after failing to meet lofty analyst expectations.

facts.fact: Wall Street futures and major indices fell, with the Nasdaq leading losses, while European markets also traded lower.
The US 10-year Treasury yield rose back toward 5.33%, near multi-decade highs, and the 30-year yield crossed 5.71%.
Brent crude oil prices surged past $104 per barrel and WTI rose above $91.50 due to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and production halts in the Gulf of Mexico.
US weekly jobless claims fell to 197,000, indicating a strong labor market, which could support further Fed rate hikes as signaled by Governor Christopher Waller.
Goldman Sachs upgraded Palantir to 'Buy' with a target price of $230, citing the global shift toward 'Sovereign AI'.
Broadcom is reportedly working to arrange over $50 billion in funding to develop custom AI chips for OpenAI.
Amazon is shifting its hardware strategy under CEO Andy Jassy, abandoning its cheap Fire tablets in favor of premium Alexa-branded tablets priced between $230 and $550.
Wolfspeed secured a $1.5 billion, 30-year loan from the Pentagon for domestic manufacturing, with the DoD receiving options for up to 7.5% of the company's shares.
Samsung Electronics reported a ninefold increase in quarterly operating profit to $80 billion, but its stock fell after missing analyst expectations.
